questions.question: How do data-* attributes work on the JavaScript side?
questions.answer: data-* values are readable via element.dataset with kebab-case converted to camelCase, e.g. data-user-id becomes dataset.userId. Values are always strings, so parse numbers, and never store secrets because HTML is public.

questions.question: What is special about template content?
questions.answer: template markup is parsed but inert: it is not rendered, and its images/scripts do not load. Access it via template.content, a DocumentFragment, and clone with cloneNode(true) before inserting.

questions.question: When should you use picture instead of srcset on img?
questions.answer: picture with source is for art direction or format fallback (AVIF/WebP/JPEG) and must end with a fallback img. srcset on img alone is for resolution switching at different widths/DPRs.

questions.question: What are the tradeoffs of contenteditable and native drag-and-drop?
questions.answer: contenteditable has no name, validation, or submission and needs ARIA plus syncing. Drag-and-drop needs dataTransfer handlers and has no keyboard equivalent by default, so provide buttons or menus as alternatives.

questions.question: What are custom elements and popover?
questions.answer: Custom elements are author-defined hyphenated tags with lifecycle callbacks (connectedCallback etc.) registered via customElements.define. popover is a native top-layer popup toggled by popovertarget, with light dismiss and Escape support.

questions.question: Create a reusable card template and clone it for Kakade with a name and role.
Why should the hero image not use loading=lazy?
questions.answer: Lazy loading delays the largest contentful paint image until it nears the viewport, which can hurt LCP. Keep above-the-fold hero images eager and lazy-load only offscreen images.

questions.question: Why is a canvas-only chart inaccessible, and what is the fix?
questions.answer: Canvas draws pixels with no DOM nodes, so screen readers get nothing. Provide an aria-label, a text summary, or a data table with the same values; SVG is an alternative when the graphic should be DOM.
